header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:egy:tla:sawmedizin:london-medical-papyrus-bm-ea-10059:translit, from the Thesaurus Linguae Aegyptiae (2018), in Simon Schweitzer's AED-TEI (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. notes.1.163: The Keftiu are usually taken to be Cretans; 1.164 is the foreign-language incantation, given in transcription. gꜣš may be a reed; ꜥwꜣyt is perhaps a fermented or rotting substance (ꜥwꜣ 'rot, ferment'); mwyt taken as urine; šbt is marked doubtful in the edition and unidentified.
notes.1.407: wḏꜣw taken as 'remedy, healing'; it could also be an amulet. 'On all its ways' is literal (perhaps 'all over it').
notes.1.1: 1.1 is badly damaged and largely obscure: ḫzd taken as 'mould, rot', rwd as 'grow', mwjj as 'urine'; 'made water' (jri.n=k mw) could also mean 'urinated'. The words from 'like the tm' on are marked ⸌ ⸍ in the edition (probably an addition) and are partly lost.
notes.1.44: nsy and nsyt are a disease or disease-demon, male and female. The end of the line is broken, and 'Nun seeks' is uncertain (perhaps 'the nsy who seeks Nun').
notes.1.140: wḫd: a pain-causing matter in the body. 1.141 is almost wholly restored. ḥmkt is an unidentified ailment. 1.143-1.144 are the foreign words of the incantation, given in transcription; the edition parses part of 1.143 as Egyptian ('Ameny ... your ka').
notes.1.393: jnn.yw taken as 'who bring'; 'the chief of the Duat' follows the editor, who removes the plural strokes. zꜣṯw is 'ground, floor'.

nodes.text: [...] in the mould(?) that grows(?), like the drinking you have done, the water of our [urine](?), like the *tm* *ꜣ[...]w* *sn[m]*(?) which [...] *kꜣ* [...]
This spell is to be said seven times.
[...] every [*nsy*-demon], every *nsyt*-demoness, because, as for the *ns[y]*, Nun [s]eeks [...] [...] him.
[I have] seen [it come about at my hand].
Conjuration of the *ḥmkt*, in the speech of the foreigner:
Conjuration of the *tj-n.t-ꜥꜣmw* (the [disease] of the Asiatics), as the Keftiu say for it:
This spell is to be said over *gꜣš* of *ꜥwꜣyt*, urine(?) and *šbt*(?).
O Horus, O Ra, O Shu, O Geb, O Osiris, O Heka, O Nun! Praise to you, great gods, who bring the chief of the Duat, who cause him to travel to the ground!
This remedy was found at night, fallen in the broad hall of the temple in Coptos, as a secret of this goddess, by the hand of the lector priest of this temple.
Now this land was in darkness,
and it was the moon that shone upon this book, on all its ways.
It was brought as a marvel to the Majesty of the King of Upper and Lower Egypt Khufu, justified.
